MATCHUPS.INTRO2: Strategies and tips for your clashes!

WAVEMANAGEMENT.SUBTITLE0: Techniques and tips for perfect lane control!
WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT1:
It is the art of strategically controlling the minion wave to gain a significant advantage in terms of map pressure, safety, as well as gold and experience gain.
Wave management is one of the most important aspects to master in the game, as it is essential on all lanes, even for a jungler.

CONTENT2.INTRO1: There are 3 types of minion waves:
CONTENT2.LIST1: <bold>Standard wave:</bold> consists of 3 melee minions and 3 ranged minions.
CONTENT2.LIST2: <bold>Cannon wave (siege):</bold> a standard wave + a cannon minion.
CONTENT2.LIST3: <bold>Super wave:</bold> a standard wave + a super minion.
CONTENT2.INTRO2:
Minions spawn for the first time at 1:05, then every 30 seconds until the end of the game.
The minion wave spawn cycle is as follows:
CONTENT2.LIST5: <bold>During the first 20 minutes:</bold> Standard wave -> Standard wave -> Cannon wave.
CONTENT2.LIST7: <bold>After 35 minutes:</bold> All waves become cannon waves.
CONTENT2.LIST8: <bold>If inhibitor is destroyed:</bold> All waves are super waves for 5 minutes (the respawn time of the inhibitor).
CONTENT2.INTRO3: <italic>Bonus info:</italic> If your team has a level and turret lead, your minions will deal more damage and take less damage from enemy minions. These bonuses increase based on the difference in levels and turrets.

CONTENT4.INTRO: The best back timings are those where you have a good window to return with <bold>key items<bold>/, <bold>minimize farm losses</bold>, and optimize your return without risking losing an advantage in lane.
CONTENT4.LIST1: The ideal time to go back depends largely on your gold. The goal is to back when you have enough gold to buy an essential component or ideally a key item that will strengthen your champion in lane. Don't wait too long to back just for "small purchases", as it can slow your progress.
CONTENT4.LIST2: If you manage to kill your opponent or force them to go back, take advantage of this window to back quickly. This allows you to return with an item advantage, increasing your chances of dominating upon your return. If the enemy leaves the lane, don't wait too long, go back as soon as possible to maximize your advantage.
CONTENT4.LIST3: Cannon waves are ideal for backing because they give you more time to return without losing too much farm. After clearing the wave of minions, this is the perfect time to back. However, make sure not to lose too many minions, even if the window is larger, and return with enough items to be competitive.
CONTENT4.LIST4: Before backing, if you have killed the enemy or if they have left, it’s crucial to shove the wave under their tower. This prevents the enemy from catching a large wave of minions and potentially freezing it in your absence. If the wave is ready to be frozen, set up a freeze under your tower, which will force the enemy to play cautiously upon your return. If you don't have enough mana or if the push takes too long, a quick back is preferable to avoid being vulnerable to a gank or falling behind in items.
CONTENT4.LIST5: If you can’t back immediately, set up a <bold>slow push</bold>. A large wave of minions crashing into the enemy tower creates a significant delay before they can react. This allows you to return to lane safely, and if the enemy is under pressure, they will have to choose between taking the wave under their tower or letting it go. You can also use this wave to set up a gank from your jungler if needed.

WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT5:
Freezing is the act of stopping the minion wave from moving, forcing the enemy to step forward to collect resources.

To maintain a freeze, you need to balance the damage your minions take with the damage dealt to enemy minions, while managing their position relative to your turret.

CONTENT6.LIST1: When the enemy deals damage to their minions (outside of last-hitting), you should adjust your damage so that all minions die around the same time, preventing the wave from pushing.
CONTENT6.LIST2: The closer the freeze is to your tower, the more enemy minions you need to leave alive to counteract the rapid arrival of your own (2-3 extra enemy minions near your tower).
CONTENT6.LIST3: If the enemy wave is too big and starts hitting your tower, you can tank it (take minion hits) to keep it in place, if you have enough health.
CONTENT6.LIST4: If the wave is too large to be tanked, reduce the number of enemy minions to maintain control of the freeze.
CONTENT6.LIST5:
The closer the wave gets to your tower, the faster your next wave will arrive. That’s why you need to leave a specific number of minions alive to freeze the lane.

This image shows how many extra minions you need to maintain a freeze.

CONTENT7.LIST1: If the enemy jungler is putting a lot of pressure on you, it's advised to freeze near your tower to farm safely and avoid ganks.
CONTENT7.LIST2: After being killed, freezing allows you to catch up on farm without overexposing yourself.
CONTENT7.LIST3: When the enemy backs without properly pushing the wave into your tower, hold the wave outside your tower to force them to overextend when they return.

WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT8:
The pros of freezing include denying the enemy minions, allowing you to gain a gold lead and forcing the enemy to overextend for farm, creating gank opportunities.
It also helps you catch up in gold and experience if you're behind.

However, a poorly executed freeze can allow the enemy to roam and create an advantage elsewhere on the map. Additionally, freezing becomes harder to maintain if the enemy has good wave clear.
WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT9: Slow pushing is the act of slowly pushing the minion wave toward the enemy tower while freeing yourself to take other actions on the map.
WAVEMANAGEMENT.SUBTITLE10: How to slow push a lane?
WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT10: Simply reduce the number of enemy minions just enough so that your wave gradually pushes forward (kill ranged minions or leave a slight minion advantage).
WAVEMANAGEMENT.SUBTITLE11: When to slow push a lane?

CONTENT11.LIST1: Before leaving your lane to assist elsewhere, ensure your wave is in a slow push so the enemy can't easily destroy your tower while you're gone.
CONTENT11.LIST2: A slow push can build into a massive wave, forcing the enemy to defend and freeing up opportunities for your team elsewhere on the map.

WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT12: Fast pushing is the technique of quickly pushing the minion wave to force the enemy to return to lane.
WAVEMANAGEMENT.SUBTITLE13: How to fast push a lane?

CONTENT13.LIST1: The goal is to clear the enemy minion wave quickly so that your minions can rapidly push towards the enemy tower.
CONTENT13.LIST2: Take out melee minions first and then focus on cannon minions to prevent your wave from slowing down.
CONTENT13.LIST3: Attack minions constantly, don't just last-hit.
CONTENT13.LIST4: Use your AoE abilities to quickly clear the wave as a whole.

WAVEMANAGEMENT.SUBTITLE14: When to fast push a lane?

CONTENT14.LIST1: If the enemy is off the lane or dead, quickly push the wave under the enemy tower to make them lose resources.
CONTENT14.LIST2: Before moving around the map, fast pushing allows you to secure your resources and free up time to assist with actions elsewhere.
CONTENT14.LIST3: Against certain champions who struggle to farm under tower, fast pushing can pressure them or force them to make mistakes.
CONTENT14.LIST4: Use your AoE abilities to quickly clear the wave as a whole.

WAVEMANAGEMENT.CONTENT15: <bold>Important:</bold> Before Fast/Slow Pushing, make sure you have enough time and map vision to avoid getting ganked.

LANING.SUBTITLE0: Dominate your opponent from the very first minutes!

CONTENT1.INTRO1: Each lane role requires mastery of combat mechanics, positioning, and resource management to surpass your direct opponent.
CONTENT1.LIST1: In top lane, it's often about prolonged duels and managing teleportation.
CONTENT1.LIST2: In mid lane, the priority is to control the map and perform efficient rotations.
CONTENT1.LIST3: In bot lane, coordination with your support and managing trades are essential.
CONTENT1.INTRO2: Mastering these aspects will allow you not only to dominate your lane but also to influence the overall course of the game.

LANING.CONTENT2:
Last hitting is essential for accumulating gold and gaining an advantage over your opponent in lane.

It consists of delivering the final blow to enemy minions to collect the gold they generate. Mastering this technique requires good timing and a precise understanding of your damage, as missing a last hit results in a loss of gold and may slow your progression.

Moreover, last hitting is crucial for effective wave management (see the chapter on Wave Management).
Use the training tool to perfect your farming and adjust your damage according to your level and equipment. The better you master last hitting, the more resources you accumulate, which gives you a clear advantage in the game – often more significant than securing kills.
LANING.CONTENT3: Trading consists of dealing damage to your opponent, either with auto-attacks or abilities.

CONTENT4.LIST1: <bold>Take advantage of enemy last-hit moments:</bold> Your opponent must kill minions to farm, becoming immobile and vulnerable at that moment. Anticipate their actions by monitoring the health of your minions and punish them with your abilities when they are about to last-hit.
CONTENT4.LIST2: <bold>Exploit enemy cooldowns:</bold> If your opponent uses abilities to farm or harass you, take advantage of the delay before they can use their spells again to engage in a trade. Baiting spells (tricking them into using them without effect) is a key tactic, which we will discuss further in the next chapter.
CONTENT4.LIST3: <bold>Pay attention to minions:</bold> Attacking a champion will provoke the enemy minions' aggro, causing them to attack you instead of your minions. Avoid prolonged fights in a large enemy minion wave, as it can quickly turn against you.
CONTENT4.LIST4: <bold>Poke the opponent:</bold> Poking consists of harassing the enemy with ranged attacks or abilities, gradually reducing their health without engaging in direct combat. This often forces the opponent to play defensively, miss minions, or consume their resources (potions, healing spells). Some champions are more effective at poking depending on their kit (for example, Ziggs or Xerath are far more effective than a Garen). Once the enemy is weakened, engage in a more aggressive fight when their situation is unfavorable.
CONTENT4.LIST5: <bold>Manage your spacing:</bold> Spacing refers to controlling the distance between you and your opponent to maximize your actions while minimizing risks. Ensure you are at the optimal range to use your abilities while staying out of range of theirs. If you're a ranged champion against a melee champion, abuse your range to harass them with auto-attacks without allowing them to farm easily.

LANING.CONTENT51:
Tip: Use bushes to break your opponent's vision during a fight. This can prevent them from targeting you with abilities or auto-attacks, while you can continue to harass them.

Any type of enemy will stop their aggression if they lose sight of you.
LANING.CONTENT5:
Trades are even more advantageous if you have a higher level than your opponent or have just gained a powerspike (power increase through a spell or item). Additionally, good wave management can help you optimize trades while minimizing resource loss.
However, be careful when engaging in a trade. An opponent near their tower with full health will be difficult to threaten. Moreover, if you start a trade and get ganked immediately after, your chances of survival will be reduced, as your abilities will be on cooldown.

Some matchups make trading more or less complicated, requiring a specific approach (specific spells on cooldown, short or long trades).
Consult the 'Matchups' section to better understand your champion's strengths and weaknesses against others.
LANING.CONTENT6: Baiting spells in lane is a strategic tactic in League of Legends. Bait means 'to lure,' and here it involves enticing your opponent to use an ability ineffectively, creating an opportunity for you.

CONTENT7.LIST1: <bold>Feign an attack:</bold> Position yourself aggressively as if you're about to engage in a fight, then back off quickly. The opponent may use a defensive or offensive spell to deter you, allowing you to re-engage while they are low on resources.
CONTENT7.LIST2: <bold>Risky positioning:</bold> Place yourself within range of a poke or control spell, but be ready to dodge or retreat quickly. If your opponent misses their spell, they become vulnerable, and you can counter-attack.
CONTENT7.LIST3: <bold>Use minions:</bold> Lure your opponent by appearing vulnerable while attempting to last-hit a low-health minion. This may entice them to waste a spell, which you can then dodge.
CONTENT7.LIST4: <bold>Simulate a lack of resources:</bold> Make your opponent believe that you are low on mana or too weak to engage in a fight. This could encourage them to play overly aggressively, giving you the opportunity to counter-attack or call your jungler for a gank.

LANING.CONTENT8: When you successfully bait a spell, it's time to exploit this window of vulnerability. If it was a key spell with a long cooldown, immediately engage in a fight or call your jungler for a kill opportunity.
LANING.CONTENT9:
Sometimes you have nothing left to do on your lane. In this case, what should you do?
If your minion wave crashes under the enemy tower and you don't have enough gold for a significant purchase at the base, it's the perfect time to go help elsewhere: this is called Roaming.

When your minion wave is under the enemy tower, your opponent is busy farming or is absent, allowing you to create a numerical advantage elsewhere on the map.

The midlane is particularly suited for roaming, as it provides quick access to other objectives and lanes. However, the support and toplaner can also roam to assist their allies or set up objectives.

CONTENT10.LIST1: <bold>Gank another lane:</bold> If your champion has good control or mobility spells, helping your allies on another lane can give them a decisive advantage.
CONTENT10.LIST2: <bold>Place vision:</bold> Place wards in the enemy jungle or around your lane to anticipate a gank.
CONTENT10.LIST3: <bold>Invade the enemy jungle:</bold> With good positioning, surprise the enemy jungler in their jungle to prevent them from collecting resources. Be careful, as their allies may come to assist; it's a safer strategy with your jungler or support.
CONTENT10.LIST4: <bold>Prepare/take an objective:</bold> Group with your allies to prepare for an important objective like a dragon or herald, placing vision around or starting the objective.

JUNGLE.SUBTITLE0: Master the game and give your team the decisive edge!

CONTENT1.INTRO1:
The jungler role is often considered the most impactful in a game of League of Legends.

The goal of a jungler is to make the best decisions to:
CONTENT1.LIST1: Help their team gain an advantage over direct opponents.
CONTENT1.LIST3: Accumulate 'free' resources by killing jungle monsters.
CONTENT1.LIST4: Anticipate ganks and movements of the enemy jungler.
CONTENT1.INTRO2: One of the main challenges of the jungler role, for both beginners and experienced players, is that success relies less on mechanical skills and more on the ability to read the game and establish an effective strategic plan.

CONTENT2.INTRO1: There are several possible jungle routes, and this decision should be made right from the loading screen:
CONTENT2.LIST1:
Full Clear: 6 Camps -> Scuttle -> Gank or Back.
This is the most common strategy in Season 14, as farming is prioritized in the current meta. However, this could change in future seasons.
CONTENT2.LIST2:
3 Camps -> Gank:
This path is useful if you want to apply early pressure and give an advantage to one of your lanes, or if your champion clears the jungle slowly. Be cautious though, as failing the gank can waste valuable time.
CONTENT2.LIST3:
1 Camp + Invade:
Start with Red or Blue, then directly invade the enemy jungle on the same side.
This should only be attempted if you're confident the enemy jungler started on the opposite side (e.g., start Red and invade Blue if the enemy starts at Red).
Be wary of potential rotations from enemy laners.

CONTENT3.INTRO1: If you opt for a full clear, the next question is: should you head bot or top? This decision depends on several factors:
CONTENT3.LIST1:
Analyze the lanes: Some lanes are more likely to push naturally than others.
For example, a Tristana will push more easily against an Ezreal due to her AoE damage. Based on this analysis, you should plan where you finish your clear: if you plan to gank bot, start your clear top, and vice versa.
CONTENT3.LIST2: <bold>Analyze summoner spells:</bold> If your top laner has Ignite and their opponent has Teleport, starting bot and ending with a gank top can be a good idea. A top laner without Teleport will have a harder time recovering from an early gank.
CONTENT3.LIST3: <bold>Analyze champions:</bold> Some champions are strong early game (like Pantheon), while others shine late game (like Veigar). Helping your late-game champions hold their lane can guarantee a long-term win. In any case, it's important to play around your team's 'carry' champions.

CONTENT4.INTRO1: There are several objectives on the map:
CONTENT4.LIST1: <bold>Top side:</bold> Gromp, Rift Herald, Baron Nashor.

JUNGLE.CONTENT5:
Securing an objective often depends on having a numerical advantage over the enemy team, which is why lane priority (PRIO) is so important. PRIO refers to your laners' ability to pressure their opponents, forcing them under their tower so they can't farm freely. This frees up your allies to move toward the river, secure objectives, or contest the enemy's objectives.

Don't hesitate to communicate the importance of PRIO to your laners before engaging in an objective. Ganking just before a key objective spawns can help secure that priority.

Avoid recalling to base right before an objective spawns. If the enemy team positions themselves before you do, it will be harder to coordinate a teamfight around that objective.

With PRIO, you can also punish the enemy jungler by invading their jungle. Whether to steal resources or kill them, this can completely disrupt the game for the enemy team, especially mentally.
JUNGLE.CONTENT6:
A 'Gank' is a maneuver where a player, often the jungler, moves to another lane to surprise an enemy and initiate a team attack.

Only Gank if you estimate there's at least an 80% chance of success; otherwise, prioritize farming. A summoner spell used by the enemy or a kill/assist is a sign of a successful gank.
Wasting time on a failed gank means falling behind in resources, which is one of the biggest struggles for a jungler.

A gank is more likely to succeed if your ally's wave is pushed or if the enemy is overextended. In this case, the enemy will have to move forward to farm, making them vulnerable to an attack. A successful gank is one where you secure a kill or force the enemy to burn summoner spells like Flash.

Frequently use your sweeper trinket to clear vision and maximize your chances of a successful gank. If you're spotted, the gank will likely fail.

CONTENT7.LIST2: <bold>Lane / Counter Gank:</bold> Wait in the lane bushes to surprise the enemy or anticipate an enemy gank.
CONTENT7.LIST3: <bold>Dives:</bold> If the enemy is under their tower with low health, and your wave is crashing under the tower, consider a dive with your laner.

CONTENT8.LIST1: Replace your trinket with a sweeper on your first back.
CONTENT8.LIST2: If you're playing power-farming/late-game champions (e.g., Shyvana, Lillia), focus more on farming than ganking.
CONTENT8.LIST3: Be mindful of your jungle timings to avoid disorganizing the monster respawns.
CONTENT8.LIST4: Focus on winning lanes. Don't waste time on losing lanes to avoid jeopardizing the whole game.
CONTENT8.LIST5: While farming, keep an eye on the map and analyze the waves. Use this time to call out the enemy jungler's positions if possible.
CONTENT8.LIST6: Communicate with your teammates via pings and chat. This improves coordination for objectives or ganks.

GAME.SUBTITLE0: Master the basics for a deeper understanding of the game!

CONTENT1.INTRO0:
Understanding champion stats is crucial for effective itemization.
Each stat influences how a champion performs in combat, and knowing how they interact with items can make a significant difference in your strategic decisions.

In this section, we will examine each stat in detail, explaining how they impact your gameplay and how to use them to select the best items for each situation.
CONTENT1.LIST1: <bold>Attack Damage (AD):</bold> Primarily used by ADCs, assassins, and bruisers, AD increases the physical damage of basic attacks and certain abilities.
CONTENT1.LIST2: <bold>Ability Power (AP):</bold> Used by mages, supports, and some assassins, AP enhances magic damage and utility effects (healing, shields).
CONTENT1.LIST3: <bold>Attack Speed (AS):</bold> Refers to how quickly your champion attacks per second. An attack speed of 1.5 means you auto-attack 1.5 times each second.
CONTENT1.LIST4: <bold>Cooldown Reduction (CDR):</bold> Reduces ability cooldowns and determines how quickly your spells become available again. CDR is not calculated linearly with CDR, becoming less effective in terms of gold as you buy more.
CONTENT1.LIST5: <bold>Critical Strike Chance:</bold> Refers to the probability of landing a critical hit, which deals 75% extra damage (not counting modifiers like Infinity Edge).
CONTENT1.LIST6: <bold>Movement Speed:</bold> Indicates how quickly your champion moves.
CONTENT1.LIST7: <bold>Tenacity:</bold> While not as straightforward as other stats, it reduces the duration of all crowd control (CC) except for knock-ups, sleep, vision reduction, stasis (Bard's ultimate), and suppression.
CONTENT1.LIST8: <bold>Health / Resource Regeneration:</bold> Health regeneration is the amount of health a champion restores per second, while resource regeneration is the amount of mana or energy a champion restores per second.
CONTENT1.LIST9: <bold>Life Steal / Omnivamp:</bold> Life steal is the percentage of health restored based on your basic attacks and impact effects. Omnivamp is similar but includes all types of damage, including abilities.
CONTENT1.LIST10:
Armor / Magic Resistance: Armor and magic resistance reduce physical and magic damage, respectively. However, many overlook that these defensive stats have diminishing returns. In other words, the more you stack these stats, the less effective they become.
Therefore, it is often unwise to stack only armor or MR, even against a full AD or AP team. Sometimes it is better to invest in items that offer other benefits, like health points, or even offensive or utility options.
CONTENT1.LIST11: <bold>Armor Penetration / Lethality:</bold> Armor penetration reduces a percentage of enemy armor, while lethality ignores a fixed value. The armor reduction value from lethality increases with lethality items but also through the champion's level. Generally, ADCs opt for armor penetration to better handle tanks, while assassins favor lethality for targeting more fragile enemies. If an assassin aims for a target with low armor, the fixed lethality proves more effective. Conversely, other champions prefer armor penetration against enemies with high defense.
CONTENT1.LIST12: <bold>Magic Penetration:</bold> Magic penetration works similarly to armor penetration and lethality. It divides into two types: flat reduction and percentage reduction.

CONTENT2.LIST2: Raw damage applied over time after each attack.

CONTENT3.LIST1: Percentage mana regeneration (also works for champions using energy).

CONTENT4.LIST1: Vision in the area (but not true vision).
CONTENT4.LIST2: Movement speed bonus for allies entering the shrine.

CONTENT5.LIST1: <bold>Chemtech Dragon:</bold> Gain tenacity and healing/shielding effectiveness.
CONTENT5.LIST2: <bold>Cloud Dragon:</bold> Gain slow resistance and out-of-combat movement speed.
CONTENT5.LIST3: <bold>Hextech Dragon:</bold> Gain haste and attack speed.
CONTENT5.LIST4: <bold>Mountain Dragon:</bold> Gain armor and magic resistance.
CONTENT5.LIST5: <bold>Infernal Dragon:</bold> Gain attack damage and ability power.
CONTENT5.LIST6: <bold>Ocean Dragon:</bold> Restores missing health every 5 seconds.
CONTENT5.LIST7: <bold>Elder Dragon:</bold> Bonus raw damage on all abilities, increases Dragon bonuses by 50%, and the buff expires after 2:30 minutes or upon death.

GAME.CONTENT6:
Killing Baron Nashor grants all living teammates a buff for 180 seconds.

This buff provides bonus attack damage, ability power, improved recall, and an aura that significantly enhances nearby minion power. Minions gain overall movement speed, range, damage, and projectile speed. With this buff, cannon minions can hit an enemy tower without being in its range.
GAME.CONTENT7:
Killing the Rift Herald drops the Herald's Eye at the entrance of the pit for 20 seconds. It can be picked up by a team member and is used to re-summon it. Once summoned, it can be used to push down a lane. Near a tower, it charges and dashes into the tower, dealing massive damage. It is also possible to ride the Herald to charge directly in a direction.

The Herald only appears once per game and disappears at 19:45, or at 19:55 if it is in combat. Baron Nashor appears in its place at 20:00.
GAME.CONTENT8:
Killing a Void Rift grants gold and experience to all team members, as well as the 'Void Touch' buff. 'Void Touch' inflicts additional damage over time on structures, and for each stack beyond the fourth, team members also receive the 'Void Hunger' buff, which will summon allied Voidlings to help destroy enemy turrets.

The Void Rift camp consists of a group of 3 Void Rifts. There can be a maximum of two spawn groups in a given game. The camp disappears at 13:45 or at 13:55 if it is in combat. A second group of Void Rifts will only spawn if the first has been eliminated before 9:45. The Rift Herald appears in the same location at 14:00.

MECANICS.SUBTITLE0: Get better and hit the opposing goals more effectively!
MECANICS.CEILINGSHOT_STEPS: Roll the ball towards a wall (without bouncing).;Follow the ball until it passes the round part of the wall.;Jump and boost at the moment of impact on the ball to reach the ceiling;Drift;Drop to keep the flip or jump from the ceiling;Hit the ball
MECANICS.CEILINGSHOT_EXPLICATION:
When the ball is high, it is often possible to use the ceiling to attack in a more unpredictable way than usual.
The ceiling shot allows you to be more comfortable with the ceiling, in addition to opening shooting angles that are not available with traditional aerial techniques, thus offering more diversity in offensive strategies.
MECANICS.FASTAERIAL_EXPLICATION:
The fast aerial allows you to reach the ball in the air faster than other players, which can be crucial for gaining an advantage during aerial duels.
Whether defending a shot or executing a quick attack, the fast aerial is a versatile technique that overall improves a player's performance.
MECANICS.WAVEDASH_STEPS: Slight jump;Air roll so the car is parallel to the ground;Lift the car upwards;Flip to land on the ground
MECANICS.WAVEDASH_EXPLICATION:
Wave dashes allow players to gain speed quickly while conserving boost. This can be crucial for reaching the ball faster or returning to defense.
Additionally, they allow for rapid and effective direction changes, which can surprise opponents and create play opportunities.

This technique can be used in various situations, whether on the ground or on walls, providing great flexibility in gameplay.
MECANICS.WALLTOAIRDRIBBLE_STEPS: Roll the ball towards a wall (without bouncing).;Follow the ball until it surpasses the round part of the wall.;Touch the ball and lift off just after that touch.;Aerial roll to straighten out.;Follow the ball in the air while managing your boost (aim for under the ball to keep it airborne as long as possible).;Aim for the opposing goals.
MECANICS.WALLTOAIRDRIBBLE_EXPLICATION:
This technique is a fundamental element of Rocket League, essential throughout your progression, regardless of your rank. It is particularly effective for surprising defenders, due to the multiple touches of the ball it involves.

However, avoid using it if an opponent is heading towards you before you reach the wall or if they are already on the wall. Additionally, if the ball bounces or is at supersonic speed (max speed), executing this technique will be more challenging.
MECANICS.HALFFLIP_STEPS: Jump;Backflip (Dash back: Joystick down + Jump);Cancel the backflip (Joystick up halfway through the flip animation to keep the car parallel to the ground);Air roll
MECANICS.HALFFLIP_EXPLICATION:
This is simply the best movement to return to defense (or attack) when your car is facing the wrong direction, while remaining dynamic on the field.
You will encounter a moment in every match where the half flip is crucial, such as during a bump, a poor challenge against an opponent, or repositioning after a bad decision, etc.
MECANICS.FLICK_DIAGONALBACKFLIP_STEPS: Jump;Turn horizontally to the right and vertically slightly upward;Left air roll;Diagonal back-left flick
MECANICS.FLICK_DIAGONALBACKFLIP_EXPLICATION:
This flick surprises your opponent due to its quick execution and keeps you well-positioned to return to defense efficiently.

Generally, it is advantageous to trigger it when you are at midfield; with some practice, this will be the perfect distance for the ball to be on target while remaining in a zone that allows for both defensive plays and aggressive follow-ups.

Technically, your main goal will be to initiate this flick with the ball in front of your car.
Simply turn your car slightly in one direction, combined with an air roll, and flick in the opposite direction (if you turn your car to the right of the ball, the flick will be triggered to the back left with the joystick: the ball will then go high to the left).

As you can see, in addition to quick execution, the directional change (unlike a front flick, for example) enhances the surprise effect of your offensive play (e.g., I dribble towards the opponent's goal on the right post side, I trigger this flick to the right of the ball, and the ball suddenly goes to the opponent's top corner left).
MECANICS.PINCH_KUXIR_STEPS: Roll the ball on the ground towards a wall, from the middle of your side;Jump towards the ball to impact it as it rolls on the wall (and not into the round part of the wall);Hit the ball slightly from the side opposite to the opposing goal;Flip into the wall at the moment of impact between the ball and the car.
MECANICS.PINCH_KUXIR_EXPLICATION:
Like many mechanics, this one can have a surprising effect, transforming a defense into a counter-attack or even a goal almost instantly. If you manage to master this pinch at least a bit, you can make a clearance that allows you to reposition yourself.

This pinch should not be attempted if your opponent is close to you or as close to the ball as you are; they can anticipate and counter you, which can play against you since you are in your half. Ideally, your opponent should also not be already positioned in defense in their goal: 90% of the time, you will just return the ball to them.

The best scenario is when you manage to accelerate the ball to one side while your opponent is taking the boost from the opposite side or is behind you.
MECANICS.MUSTYFLICK_STEPS: Jump after the bounce to send the ball up while following it (like an Air Dribble);Turn the car backward, boosting if necessary to avoid touching the ball;Perform a backflip
MECANICS.MUSTYFLICK_EXPLICATION:
The Musty Flick is an advanced mechanic that allows you to propel the ball with speed and an angle that is difficult for your opponent to anticipate. What makes this move particularly fearsome is the element of surprise it generates: when your car flips backward, the opponent generally expects you to land with the ball. However, triggering the flick at this precise moment catches your opponent off guard by sending the ball sharply upward.

This mechanic is not limited to simple execution; if you master 'Cancel Flips,' you can slightly delay the flick timing, giving you even more control and increasing your shot's power. This makes the action even more unpredictable and difficult to counter, adding an extra dimension to your offensive play.

HOME.SUBBIENVENUE: The ultimate hub for competitive gamers who want to improve
HOME.CONTENT1:
In the gaming world, the ascent to the top can often seem like an obstacle-filled journey, especially for beginner players. Generally, 85% of players are ranked Diamond or below, which is why I came up with the idea of creating a platform dedicated to those who aspire to improve their skills and progress in their game.

My goal with TeamUpp is simple: to gather, in one place, all the information you need to progress in your favorite games. No more struggling to find answers to your questions or navigating through different sources. Here, you will find structured guides, clear tips, and strategies directly accessible for several competitive games.

I want to make learning simple, effective, and above all accessible to everyone.
HOME.CONTENT2: Instead of spending hours digging through forums or browsing scattered videos on YouTube, TeamUpp gathers everything a beginner player needs in one place. Whether you are new or just want to refine your skills, we provide you with practical guides, tips, and strategies, carefully organized for smooth and intuitive navigation.
HOME.CONTENT3: We believe that every player deserves a chance to shine. That’s why we are committed to making learning accessible and engaging. Our content is designed to be easily understandable, even for those who have never touched a competitive game before.
HOME.CONTENT4: In addition to our resources, TeamUpp aims to be a true community. We encourage interaction among players, allowing everyone to share experiences, exchange tips, and support each other in their quest for progress. Together, we build an environment where everyone can thrive and feel supported.
HOME.TITLE5: Ready to Elevate Your Game Level?
HOME.CONTENT5:
Join us today and discover how TeamUpp can transform your gaming experience. Together, let’s make your gaming journey a rewarding and successful adventure.

Your ascent begins here!

CONTACT:
Hi there! 👋

I’m Hato, the sole person behind the TeamUpp project.
Convinced that we can create something impactful for the world of competitive gaming, and help every player by giving them the tools to improve, I’m pouring all my energy and efforts into this project (even though it’s really tough going solo).

You’ll often find me live on Twitch 🔴, where the main content is gaming with viewers 🎮, chatting 💬, and interacting with them 🤙 (of course, everyone is welcome to join).
I’ve also set up a Discord server, so we can create a real community, exchange ideas, and support each other as passionate gamers 🫶.

Your feedback is crucial to help me succeed. So if you have any questions, ideas, or just want to share your thoughts, feel free to reach out to me on the social platforms below (especially Instagram).
I’d be really happy to chat with you! 🤗
